name: Vantage Lighthouse campus (Stargate Port Washington)
summary: Vantage Data Centers is building Lighthouse, a four-building campus on 672 acres on Port Washington's north side in Wisconsin, for Oracle and OpenAI under the Stargate program. OpenAI, Oracle and Vantage announced it as a Stargate site in October 2025, with close to 1 GW of capacity and completion targeted for 2028. Vantage now lists 902 MW, while local reporting and analyst Epoch AI cite 1.3 GW. The investment is reported at about $15 billion. Two buildings had topped out by mid-2026. We Energies supplies power; an Oracle subsidiary sued state regulators in June 2026 over financial-security rules, and in October 2026 We Energies proposed an Oracle share of nuclear output, pending approval.

metrics.note: Announced as close to a gigawatt of AI capacity across four data centers.
Vantage's locations page lists the campus at 902 MW total without saying whether this is IT or facility power.
Local reporting on the 2025 city approval said the campus would use 1.3 GW of power; it does not reconcile this with the 902 MW figure.
Analyst estimate, not a company disclosure: Epoch AI's projection of total facility power.
Figure given by Vantage when the city approved the developer's agreement; Vantage said it was likely to grow.
Total land Vantage bought on the city's north side; only the southern 672 acres are being developed.
The 2025 plan described two buildings of about 560,000 sq ft and two of about 719,000 sq ft.
Mostly union jobs. In mid-2026 about 1,700 workers were on site, expected to reach about 5,000 going into winter.
Figure from the October 2025 announcement and repeated in September 2026 coverage; in August 2025 Vantage spoke of about 300 long-term employees.

milestones.note: Port Washington approved a developer's agreement with Vantage for the campus.
OpenAI, Oracle and Vantage announced the campus as a Stargate site.
Analyst estimate, not a company disclosure: Epoch AI dates the start from satellite imagery showing foundation work by February 2026; ground preparation may have begun earlier.
An Oracle subsidiary sued Wisconsin utility regulators in Ozaukee County court over tightened financial-security requirements for data center customers of We Energies.
Second of four buildings topped out; the project was reported to be about 12 to 15 percent complete.
We Energies proposed letting Oracle subscribe to 10 to 20 percent of Point Beach nuclear plant output to help serve the campus, pending regulatory approval.

power_sources.description: Supplied by We Energies, with Vantage saying no cost of acquiring the energy will be passed on to other utility customers.
Roughly 70 percent of the campus supply is to come from zero-emission sources, which analyst Epoch AI lists as solar, wind and battery storage, with the rest offset through purchased credits.
Wind is part of the 70 percent clean supply mix described for the campus by analyst Epoch AI.
Battery storage is part of the 70 percent clean supply mix described for the campus by analyst Epoch AI.
Proposed subscription by Oracle to 10 to 20 percent of Point Beach nuclear plant generation through We Energies, awaiting Public Service Commission approval.

notes: Capacity figures differ by source and basis: close to 1 GW at announcement, 902 MW on Vantage's site, 1.3 GW of power in local reporting, and a 1.3 GW facility-power projection from analyst Epoch AI that is not a company disclosure. Reported investment rose from at least $8 billion in August 2025 to about $15 billion by mid-2026. Related-story headlines on news pages suggest Oracle later dropped its lawsuit, but no article opened here reports that.
